empty.noBudgetDescription: Go to Create budget to be able to add transactions.
empty.noTransactionsDescription: Import a CSV statement from your bank — transactions will be categorized automatically, and the uncertain ones will go to review.
empty.noExpensesInPeriod: No expenses in the selected period

source.title: Account
source.description: Choose the account the transactions will be booked to.

file.title: CSV file
file.description: Choose the statement exported from your banking app.

preview.title: Preview
preview.description: Check the imported transactions and their categories.

source.heading: CSV file import
source.caption: Start by picking the account the statement came from. We read the file in the matching format — you do not have to configure anything.
source.bankPlaceholder: The bank the statement came from
source.budgetPlaceholder: The budget the changes will be saved to

noBudget.title: No budget in the application
noBudget.body: You need to create a budget before you can import from a bank.

file.heading: Statement file
file.caption: Upload the CSV exported from your bank. Nothing is saved yet — we will first show you what we read from it.
file.drop: Click or drag the file here
file.hint: A single CSV file. The format follows from the bank you picked.
file.working: Reading the file and assigning categories…

preview.heading: Transaction preview
preview.caption: See how we read your transactions and which categories we gave them. The ones we were unsure about are marked "needs review" — fix them now or later. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
preview.removeConfirm: Remove the selected rows ({{count}})? They will not be imported.
preview.acceptConfirm: Accept the suggestions for {{count}} rows? The categories stay the same, but you become their author — the rows leave the queue and will train the model.

done.heading: Summary
done.caption: Your budget is ready. From now on every expense shows how much is left in its category.
done.pendingReview: {{count}} transactions are waiting for category review.
done.duplicates: Skipped {{count}} rows that were already in the database.

filters.budgetsNote: Several budgets selected. If the same statement was imported into more than one, the tiles count the same money more than once.

selection.editDisabledHint: Inline editing only works for the on-page selection, not for the whole matching set.

noBudget.title: No budget available
noBudget.description: Go to Create budget to be able to add and browse transactions.

noTransactions.title: No transactions yet
noTransactions.description: Import a CSV statement from your bank to see transactions here.

noFilterResults.title: No transaction matches the selected filters.

bulkSetCategory.title: Bulk category assignment
bulkSetCategory.info: Once accepted, {{count}} transactions will change. If needed, you can retrain the model on the new categories in settings.

discardEdits.description: Changing the page, a filter, or the sort order will discard the edited, unsaved rows.

createBudget.title: Create a budget
createBudget.caption: Let us set up your monthly budget. You will set category limits afterwards on the “Spending limits” screen.
createBudget.name: Budget name

basics.title: Basic information
basics.description: Set the budget parameters so transactions can be booked against it

settings.title: Application settings
settings.intro: Set up the accounts you import statements from, plus the categories and rules we use to sort your transactions.

training.caption: Training data
training.description: The model learns from the base file and from your category corrections. Here you can see exactly what it learns from, and retrain it.

composition.corrected: {{count}} of your corrections changed the category of examples already in the set. The set does not grow, but the model will learn something different from them.
composition.duplicates: Skipped {{count}} corrections already present in the base file with the same category — otherwise the same examples would count twice.

training.newCorrections: {{count}} corrections since the last training. The model has not seen them yet.
training.upToDate: The model has learned from every correction so far.

recategorizeConfirm.description: The current model and rules will be applied to transactions already in the database. Categories you set manually, and confirmed ones, are left untouched. Transactions the model has no opinion about go back to the review queue.

recategorizeReport.title: Categories recalculated
recategorizeReport.body: Checked {{examined}} transactions: {{recategorized}} changed category, {{movedToReview}} of which went back to the review queue.

report.title: Training finished
report.body: {{rows}} examples, {{categories}} categories. Overall accuracy {{micro}}, per-category average {{macro}}.

training.metricsCaveat: Accuracies are indicative, not a quality gate. Every training splits a different set into train and test because the set grows — a higher number than last time does not by itself mean a better model.

distribution.caption: Distribution by category
distribution.emptyWarning: {{count}} categories have no examples at all — the model will never pick them.

history.caption: Training history
history.empty: No training has been run from this screen yet.

restoreConfirm.description: The active model will be swapped. No version is removed, so you can go back the other way.

training.restoreSuccess: The selected model version is now active.

budgets.caption: Budget list
budgets.description: A budget is the rule set the processes around imported transactions work on. Manage it here.
budgets.empty: You do not have any budget yet.
budgets.error: The operation failed. Check your connection and try again.

edit.title: Edit budget
edit.name: Name
edit.balanceHint: Derived from the opening balance and the transactions — it cannot be set directly.
edit.recalculationTitle: Changing the opening balance recalculates the whole budget
edit.recalculation: The balance for every day is counted from this value, so the entire chart shifts, not a single number.

delete.header: Are you sure you want to delete the budget "{{name}}"?
delete.description: After deletion this stays reversible for {{days}} days. After that the budget is gone from the system for good.

disableConfirm.header: Are you sure you want to switch off the budget "{{name}}"?
disableConfirm.description: A switched-off budget stops accepting new data (imports and transactions), but stays fully visible — you can still edit, reset, and delete it.

errors.network: Could not reach the server. Please try again.

savings.title: Savings goals
savings.goalEnded: Goal ended. The history of proofs stays.
savings.raiseSuggestion: You have {{count}} months with a proof. In months with one-off expenses the budget carried roughly {{headroom}} above the goal.

chart.caption: How much you saved each month
chart.legend: Bar = saved that month · line = your goal · dot = month with a one-off expense
chart.noGoalHint: Set a goal to see the threshold on the chart.

noGoal.title: You have not set a savings goal yet.
noGoal.body: Set the amount you want to put aside every month — only then can I tell you whether you keep it up despite one-off expenses.

noLargeExpense.title: You have not marked any one-off expense.
noLargeExpense.body: Without them I cannot tell a hard month from an ordinary one, so no proof can appear. Mark them in the transaction list.

proof.title: You saved {{amount}} in {{month}} too — a month with {{oneOff}} of one-off expenses.
proof.body: This goal is safe. Months with a proof: {{count}}.

missed.title: {{month}} fell {{missing}} short of the goal.
missed.body: There were {{oneOff}} of one-off expenses. This is information, not a judgement — a proof appears in a month where the goal holds despite them.

noSavingsSeen.title: I cannot see any savings deposits.
noSavingsSeen.body: Saving is recognised by the “Oszczędności” category. If your transfer is described differently it will not be counted — check the category in the transaction list.

months.caption: Months
months.notOneOff: This was not a one-off expense
months.empty: No transactions in this budget yet.

modal.title: Set a savings goal
modal.floorNote: The goal is a floor, not a ceiling — I check whether you saved AT LEAST that much.
modal.historyNote: Changing the amount does not overwrite history: the previous goal ends with a date and older proofs still refer to it. Raising applies from this month, lowering from the next.
modal.startedOnNote: Only for the first goal — this is what gives your past months a verdict. Later changes are dated by the app itself.

endConfirm.description: The goal is ended with a date, not deleted — past proofs will still refer to the amount that was in force back then.

clearOneOffConfirm.description: {{count}} transactions in {{month}} will lose the marking. A month that was a proof only thanks to them will stop being one.

errors.loadFailed: Could not load the savings data

reservations.title: All reservations
reservations.tileEmpty: No reservations yet. Name an upcoming expense and I will set money aside for it.
reservations.summary: {{reserved}} PLN reserved · {{settled}} PLN settled · free funds {{free}} PLN
reservations.summaryOver: {{reserved}} PLN reserved · {{settled}} PLN settled · no free funds
reservations.balanceNote: Savings account balance: {{balance}} PLN. Computed as deposits minus withdrawals in the “Savings” category — not an account balance, so it excludes the opening balance and interest.
reservations.coveredBy: At your current monthly goal the rest will be collected by {{month}}.
reservations.deleted: Reservation deleted. Free funds are back.

overReserved.title: Reservations exceed the account balance by {{amount}} PLN.
overReserved.body: This is not an error — you reserved more than you have saved. The nearest deadline collects first, the rest wait for what is left.

editor.name: Name
editor.queueNote: Reservations collect in order — nearest deadline first. Adding one with an earlier deadline WILL SHIFT THE QUEUE and take progress away from the others.

settleModal.title: Was this: {{name}}?
settleModal.pick: Pick the withdrawal from the savings account that closed this reservation.
settleModal.noCandidates: I see no unsettled savings withdrawal in this budget. Settling always points at a real transaction — without one, reservations would be a wish list.
settleModal.freeFundsNote: Settling closes this reservation and takes it out of the collection queue, but it does NOT increase free funds — the envelope is annual, so the amount stays committed for the whole year.
settleModal.manualNote: I never settle automatically — a mistake here closes an envelope nobody paid, and nobody would notice.

deleteConfirm.description: The amount will stop weighing on free funds and the collection queue will shift to the remaining reservations.

unsettleConfirm.description: The reservation goes back into the collection queue and the chosen withdrawal becomes available again. Free funds will not change.

reservations.freeFundsBody: Savings account balance {{balance}} PLN − {{reserved}} PLN of reservations.
reservations.balanceCaveat: The balance is computed as deposits minus withdrawals in the “Savings” category — not an account balance, so it excludes the opening balance and interest.

limits.title: Spending limits
limits.removed: Limit removed. The category has no limit from the current month on.

banner.noLimits: This budget has no limits yet.
banner.noLimitsClosed: {{month}} — the budget had no limits in this month.
banner.noLimitsBody: You set a limit for a spending category. Next to it you can see where the money goes this month — a good starting point, but you pick the amount.
banner.allFine: Every category is within its limit.
banner.closedFine: {{month}} — closed month. Every category stayed within its limit.
banner.closedBody: Showing the limits that applied in that month — not today's.
banner.uncategorized: Expenses without a category ({{count}}, {{amount}} in total) do not count towards any limit until they get one.

table.title: Category limits
table.hint: The limit applies every month in this budget · spent = categorised expenses in the selected month, including large ones
table.readOnlyHint: A past month is read-only — limits change from the current month on

unlimited.title: Spending without a limit
unlimited.hint: Categories with expenses this month that have no limit
unlimited.empty: Every category with expenses has a limit.
unlimited.note: These {{amount}} are not part of the monthly budget limit — the budget limit is the sum of category limits, nothing more.
unlimited.contextNote: This month's amounts, for context only — no limit is suggested.

editor.ceilingNote: A limit is a CEILING on a category's monthly spending — every expense counts, including large ones. The warning threshold changes the bar colour before the limit is exceeded.
editor.historyNote: A change does not rewrite history: the previous limit ends a month earlier and past months keep that amount. The monthly budget limit will be {{total}}.

removeConfirm.description: {{limit}} a month · {{spent}} spent this month. Transactions stay as they are — the category moves to “Spending without a limit” and the monthly budget limit drops to {{total}}. Past months keep this limit.
